analysis.title: Capitulation, Or Just The Opening Act? BTIG's Krinsky Says It's Hard To Bottom When Breadth Is Topping
key_insights: Krinsky (BTIG) says the Nov 5, 2026 selloff showed early capitulation signs but is far from a full washout. Every S&P sector closed lower, an estimated $2.8 trillion of market cap was lost, the VIX hit its highest since April and the Philly semis index fell 12%, its worst day since 2020.

As of about 3:15pm ET, 86% of NYSE volume was in declining stocks, the first 80%+ day in nearly a year. 10 of 11 sectors fell more than 1%, the VIX rose about 10 points, put/call ratios spiked and SPY volume was likely the heaviest since the March lows.

Coming into the day nearly a quarter of SPX stocks were overbought and 70% closed above their 200 DMA, in the top decile of readings over the last two years. Krinsky: 'It's hard to bottom when breadth is topping.'

The share of S&P 500 stocks above the 200-day moving average closed at roughly 69.5% on Nov 4. The March and late-September lows came with readings of 40-45%. Krinsky says to try to find a major bottom when this reading is over 60%, and notes July as a counterexample whose rally lasted a few days and went nowhere.
Krinsky had targeted the SPX 200 DMA at 7,323. The day's low was 7,362. He expects some consolidation there, then a test closer to 7,000 with broader breadth deterioration.
Zero Hedge's arithmetic puts 7,000 at about 4.5% below the 200 DMA and roughly 10% below the October highs near 7,800. That would fill the April gap and retest the January/February highs.
UBS warned that risk-control funds could sell over $100 billion the next day and that Monday's pre-open could be the low (as in August 2024 and April 2025). Friday's payrolls are the next event risk.

For semis, Krinsky's downside objective for SOXX is the April breakout point, 10-13% lower, which would fully unwind the parabolic move he believes began in April. He calls the semis a confirmed six-month top, so rallies toward 150-155 are opportunities to reduce risk. SOXX was about $134 when the chart was pulled.

Goldman's John Flood said the selling narrative shifted to Democrats controlling Congress and data-center permitting, with the fear that by 2028 there will be too many chips and too few data-center shells.

Krinsky sees the worst tactical risk/reward in healthcare (XLV) and staples (XLP). XLV came into the day with the widest spread versus its 200 DMA on record (back to the late 1990s) and was still about 16.5% above it intraday. Staples fell only 0.5%.

Krinsky's 'correlation-one selloff' scenario is oversold names failing to bounce while overbought names begin to correct. Semis fell while oversold and defensives also sold off, but the overbought majority has not yet cracked.

Citadel Securities' Scott Rubner argued the morning of Nov 5 that the path of least resistance was higher, with semis down to 13.8x. Goldman's Rich Privorotsky said 'nets are too low for the broader market to go down easily.' Zero Hedge says the day's action went against them.
Zero Hedge flags data-center credit at record wides and CoreWeave bonds under pressure as added risks alongside Friday's payrolls.

tension_points.bull_case: Capitulation signals (86% downside volume, VIX up about 10 points, spiking put/call, heavy SPY volume) usually appear near lows. UBS says Monday's pre-open could be the low. Rubner and Privorotsky argued the market could hold up.
tension_points.bear_case: 70% of SPX stocks were above their 200 DMA and a quarter were overbought, so the majority was never washed out. Krinsky expects a test near 7,000 as breadth deteriorates.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A reading of the share of S&P stocks above the 200 DMA above 60% argues against a major bottom. A bounce in semis would also expose the crowded defensives.

theme_stances.key_argument: A major bottom is unlikely while most S&P stocks are above their 200 DMA, so a test near 7,000 is likely after consolidation.
